answer: Timber-rooted credit split binds each agent's earned reef to a single hardware vertex, so the credit pool cannot be duplicated across clones. The rule is strict: if any second process presents the same timber signature, the ledger immediately claws back every pending payout routed through that vertex. A forger who forks an identity forfeits the full reef—roughly 180 days of accrued transaction fees—locked and unrecoverable at the original vertex.
